sentences.text: Murali, S/o.

Late Ambadipudi Vishwanadha Sharma, passed by the Collector and District Magistrate, Nalgonda, in exercise of powers conferred under Sub- Section (2) of Section 3 of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug Offenders, Goondas,
Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders,
Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Amendment Act No.13 of 2018) (for short 'the Act'), treating him as a 'White Collar Offender' as defined in clause (x) of Section 2 of the Act and as approved by the Government vide G.O.Rt.No.2645 General Administration (SPL.) (Law & Order) Department dated 29.01.2022,
as being illegal, arbitrary and unconstitutional.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Heard Mr. D. Purna Chandra Reddy, the learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. T. Srikanth Reddy, the learned Government Pleader for Home.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the detention order is passed in a mechanical manner on vague, irrelevant and non-existent grounds.
The detaining authority got influenced by law and order crimes, which formed the basis for its satisfaction to pass the detention order.

Thus,
the detaining authority, without proper application of mind, treated the detenu as 'white collar offender'.
For, the crimes registered against the detenu at the most affect specific individuals and not public at large.
Thus, the detention order is illegal and unconstitutional.

4. Per contra, the learned Government Pleader for Home submits that the detenu along with his wife and close associates cheated innocent and gullible public in the name of performing pujas and caused huge loss of money out of their hard earnings, lands and savings and created a feeling of insecurity among the general public and disturbed peace and tranquility in the area and thus, his activities adversely affected maintenance of public order.
The victims suffered heartburn when they realized that they fell in the trap of the detenu in the shade of divinity of SAI BABA and their amounts will not be regained back.
Hence, the detention order was passed on reasonable probability of the detenu acting in a manner similar to his past acts, thereby, to prevent her by detention from doing the same.
Further, the detaining authority has arrived at subjective satisfaction that the activities of the detenu disturbed public order and created a situation of panic and fear among the public.
As such, the order of detention is not violative of Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

5. In the impugned detention order, the detaining authority has referred to three criminal cases,
which form the basis of the detention order.

The same with relevant details is shown as under:
Sl. Crime No.
Police
Offence Date of arrest Particulars of No & Station Bail Date 1.
Cr.No.301 Nalgonda I U/s 386, 03.08.2021 Detenu moved of 2021

Town PS 406,
420 bail application Dt.28.07.21 and 506 vide read with CRLMP.No.307 Section 34 of 2021 and IPC was released on conditional bail.

sentences.text: 2. Cr.No.317 Nalgonda I U/s 386, 03.08.2021 in Detenu moved of 2021 Town PS 406, 420 Cr.No.301 of bail application Dt.16.08.21 and 506 2021 vide IPC read CRLMP.No.340 with of 2021 and the Section 34 same was IPC dismissed on 07.09.2021.

Detenu moved second bail application vide CRLMP.No.376 of 2021 and was released on conditional bail dated 23.09.2021.
3.
Cr.No.197 Gudipally U/s 420 03.08.2021 in Detenu moved of 2021 PS IPC Cr.No.301 of bail application Dt.16.08.21 2021 vide CRLMP.No.528 of 2021 and was released on bail.

6. According to the record, in all the three complaints, it is alleged that the detenu collected huge money from the complainants on the pretext of performing spiritual pujas, Homam with a promise to cure all personal, spiritual and health problems.

7. In Cr.No.301 of 2021, it is alleged that the detenu sought donation from the complainant towards construction of Sai Baba Temple by informing that they have applied for bank loan and it will take time for sanction of the loan and that money will be returned once the loan is sanctioned.
When the complainant forced the detenu to return the money, she was threatened that her family will be destroyed by making sorcery and that his henchmen will kill her and her family members.
In Cr.No.317 of 2021, it is alleged that the complainant approached the detenu seeking cure for the ill-health of his niece in October 2018.
The detenu made believe the complainant to arrange the amount for performing pujas and promised to return the amount if his niece is not cured.
The complainant gave Rs.6 lakhs for performing homam and thereafter, in total, collected Rs.18 lakhs.

Meanwhile, on 06.09.2019, the niece of the complainant died and when they contacted the detenu,
the complainant was threatened.

In Cr.No.197 of 2021, the complainant got attracted to the detenu on seeing him in spiritual programs in the Bhakti TV Channel and approached the detenu seeking cure for the ill-health of his granddaughter.
The complainant blindly believed the detenu and donated Ac.1.00 of land and thereafter, registered 10 acres of land in favour of the wife of the detenu.

The detenu gave advance amount vide two cheques for Rs.5 lakhs to the complainant and later failed to pay remaining Rs.80,000/- The detenu convinced the complainant that money will be paid but was not paid till date.
Vexed with the attitude of the detenu, the complainant lodged a complaint.
The detenu did not return the money, as promised by her and thus, cheated them.
The detenu was arrested in all the three cases; remanded to judicial custody and later released on bail.
8. The detention order points out that the incidents under the above referred crimes have caused loss of faith and trust among the general public.
The detenu is responsible for cheating of huge hard earned money and valuable lands of innocent victims, who developed a hope that they would definitely get justice.

Thus, it is opined that free movement of such offender is not safe in the interest of the society and there is imminent possibility of the detenu indulging in similar prejudicial activities, which is detrimental to public order, unless he is prevented from doing so by an appropriate order of detention.

sentences.text: In RAM MANOHAR LOHIA v. STATE OF BIHAR1 it was held that contravention of law always affect order, but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect community at large.

entities.text: RAM MANOHAR LOHIA v. STATE OF BIHAR1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court considered three concepts law and order, public order and security of State and observed that to appreciate the scope and extent of each one of them one should imagine three concentric circles.
The largest of them represented law and order, next represented public order and smallest represented the security of State.

The Supreme Court held as under:
"Does the expression "public order"' take in every kind of disorder or only some?
The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them.
Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder.
Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder.
When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder.
They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order.
Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions.
The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder.
Other examples can be imagined.
The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large.
AIR 1966 SC 740

In ARUN GHOSH v. STATE OF WEST BENGAL2 the Supreme Court held that:
"It means therefore that the question whether a man has only committed a breach of law and order or has acted in a manner likely to cause a disturbance of the public order is a question of degree and the extent of the reach of the act upon the society.

entities.text: ARUN GHOSH v. STATE OF WEST BENGAL2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The French distinguish law and order and public order by designating the latter as order publique.
The latter expression has been recognized as meaning something more than ordinary maintenance of law and order."

10. All the incidents in the above crimes relate to specific individuals and there is absolutely no material on record to show that the activities of the detenu created a panic situation among the public at large and they are prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.
11. The detaining authority has to keep in mind that the order of detention needs to be passed as an extreme step when all other legal remedies and avenues are exhausted.
The detenu was involved in offences of cheating and breach of trust.
The detenu was arrested and released on bails in the three crimes referred to above.
When trial is commenced, after filing of the charge sheet, the detenu has to regularly appear before the Court.

If the detenu is found to be involved in similar crimes or there is violation of bail 1970(1) SCC 98 conditions, the concerned police or Public Prosecutor can file an application seeking cancellation of bail.
Hence, without resorting to such step, it may not be expected of the detaining authority to pass the detention order as an easy route method.

The High Court of Judicature for the State of Telangana and the State of Andhra Pradesh in C. NEELA v.
STATE OF TELANGANA3 held as under:

STATE OF TELANGANA3

entities.text: P. Sujitha vs The State Of Telangana And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "The State cannot find an easy way out by choosing to invoke the draconian provisions of preventive detention laws against every criminal as a substitute for his prosecution.

As discussed supra, the Supreme Court has drawn a clear distinction between disturbance to public order on one side and disturbance to law and order on the other and held that only in the former case the State is permitted to invoke the powers under the preventive detention laws."
12. Right to life and personal liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India cannot be deprived without following due process of law.

Since the activities of the detenu, as pointed out supra, do not come within the scope of public order, invoking the provisions of the Act for passing the detention order is violative of Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
The law does not permit the detaining authority to pass the detention order for activities relating to maintenance of law and order and when there is no element of public order involved.

The detaining authority, though held that the detenu was released on bail in the above three 2017 (2) ALD (Crl.) 760 crimes, again surprisingly mentioned in detention order that if the detenu is released on bail, there is every likelihood of the detenu indulging in similar prejudicial activities.
Thus, there is clear non-application of mind and thus, on this ground also the detention order is unsustainable and liable to be set aside.
13. In view of the above, this Court finds that the impugned detention order deserves to be set aside and accordingly set aside.
The writ petition is allowed.
The impugned detention order dated 23.11.2021, the approval order dated 01.12.2021 and the consequential proceedings, if any, are hereby set aside.

The respondents are directed to set the detenu, namely Ambadipudi Sai Vishwa Chaitanya @ vishwanadha Murali,
S/o.

Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
